Also: The 38th AAAI Conference at the Vancouver Convention Centre — the 4th-ranked AI venue by h5-index. This report covers 13 papers, including a Waabi keynote.

LLMs dominate, but the focus is reliability — citations, symbolic reasoning, grounding and rationality limits — alongside multimodal foundation models in medicine, physics-informed generative simulation, and interpretable autonomous-driving AI.

Insight 01 · Reliable LLM reasoning & generation

Chain-of-Thought Improves Text Generation with Citations in LLMs

CoT + Citation Insurance Mechanism · AAAI 2024
Goal

Enable LLMs to generate text with accurate citations, improving answer correctness and citation quality.

Challenge

LLMs hallucinate and struggle to synthesize and properly cite across multiple documents.

Method
  • Chain-of-Thought prompting to synthesize answers with citations
  • Four prompting strategies: Vanilla, Summ, Snippet, Oracle
  • A Citation Insurance Mechanism (CIM) detects and fixes missing citations (LLM- and IR-based)
Novelty

Combines CoT reasoning with a citation-insurance mechanism to guarantee citations.

Impact

Consistent gains in citation recall/precision, correctness and fluency on ALCE across six LLMs (13–70B).

[1] “Chain-of-Thought Improves Text Generation with Citations in Large Language Models,” AAAI 2024.
Insight 02 · Reliable LLM reasoning & generation

Can LLMs Serve as Rational Players in Game Theory?

LLMs as rational players · AAAI 2024
Goal

Assess whether LLMs can act as rational players in social-science game experiments.

Challenge

Rationality requires building desires, refining beliefs under uncertainty, and taking optimal actions.

Method
  • Three classic games: dictator, rock-paper-scissors, ring-network
  • Evaluate desire, belief refinement and optimal action
  • Systematic analysis across LLMs including GPT-4
Novelty

A systematic framework for probing the rationality boundaries of LLMs in game theory.

Impact

LLMs show basic desire but struggle with belief refinement; GPT-4 is sometimes human-like — guidance for social-science use.

[2] “Can Large Language Models Serve as Rational Players in Game Theory? A Systematic Analysis,” AAAI 2024.
Insight 03 · Reliable LLM reasoning & generation

Frugal LMs Trained to Invoke Symbolic Solvers (SYRELM)

SYRELM · AAAI 2024
Goal

Achieve parameter-efficient, interpretable arithmetic reasoning without massive LLMs.

Challenge

LLMs are resource-intensive and unreliable for arithmetic reasoning.

Method
  • Translate natural-language questions into formal language (e.g. Python) for a symbolic solver
  • Fine-tune a small LM with a Low-Rank Adapter (LoRA)
  • Optimize with PPO using a reasoning-specific reward (compilation, variable/operator match, answer error)
Novelty

A frugal LM + symbolic solver, with middle-school-math pedagogy shaping the reward.

Impact

Strong arithmetic gains with a small, accessible, interpretable alternative to huge LLMs.

[3] “Frugal LMs Trained to Invoke Symbolic Solvers Achieve Parameter-Efficient Arithmetic Reasoning,” AAAI 2024.
Insight 04 · LLM agents & applied foundation models

PromptGAT: Sim-to-Real Transfer for Traffic Signal Control with Prompt Learning

PromptGAT · AAAI 2024
Goal

Close the sim-to-real gap for reinforcement-learning traffic signal control.

Challenge

Grounded Action Transformation (GAT) struggles with unobserved states; prompt learning was untried for sim-to-real.

Method
  • Use LLMs to improve GAT's forward (dynamics) model
  • Prompt-based grounded action transformation aligns policy with realistic dynamics
  • Evaluate on four traffic-signal-control scenarios
Novelty

First to bring prompt learning (LLMs) into sim-to-real grounded action transformation.

Impact

Mitigates the RL sim-to-real performance gap for urban traffic control.

[4] “Prompt to Transfer: Sim-to-Real Transfer for Traffic Signal Control with Prompt Learning,” AAAI 2024.
Insight 05 · LLM agents & applied foundation models

Building Conversational Artifacts for APIs and RPAs

Conversational artifacts · AAAI 2024
Goal

Make API/RPA automation usable by non-technical users via conversational digital assistants.

Challenge

Domain knowledge and LLM fine-tuning are costly (esp. for SMEs); LLMs at runtime risk trust and indemnity.

Method
  • Human-guided authoring of API services as chatbot skills
  • LLMs used only in the build phase — pre-generate and review conversational artifacts
  • Intent classification, question generation and Next-Best-Agent via ChromaDB + MiniLM
Novelty

Pre-generated, reviewed artifacts remove LLMs from user interactions entirely.

Impact

Lower build effort, trustworthy automation and an automated DevOps deployment pipeline.

[5] “Building Conversational Artifacts to Enable Digital Assistant for APIs and RPAs,” AAAI 2024.
Insight 06 · LLM agents & applied foundation models

PathAsst: A Generative Foundation AI Assistant for Pathology

PathAsst · AAAI 2024
Goal

Build a multimodal generative foundation assistant for diagnostic and predictive pathology.

Challenge

Pathology multimodal models are limited by scarce tailored data and model frameworks.

Method
  • Collect 207K pathology image-text pairs + 180K ChatGPT instruction samples (PathCap, PathInstruct)
  • Build PathCLIP, a pathology-dedicated CLIP model
  • Integrate PathCLIP with Vicuna-13B, plus eight pathology-specific sub-models
Novelty

A pathology-dedicated CLIP + instruction-tuned assistant toward pathology AGI.

Impact

Stronger diagnostic and predictive analytics on digitized histopathology.

[6] “PathAsst: A Generative Foundation AI Assistant towards AGI of Pathology,” AAAI 2024.
Insight 07 · LLM agents & applied foundation models

Bootstrapping Cognitive Agents with a Large Language Model

LLM-bootstrapped cognitive agents · AAAI 2024
Goal

Combine LLM common-sense with a cognitive architecture for embodied tasks.

Challenge

Cognitive architectures need knowledge; LLMs hallucinate and need grounding.

Method
  • Separate knowledge generation (LLM) from application (cognitive architecture)
  • Generate English action descriptions → executable Python production rules; a critic LLM improves them
  • Production reinforcement updates utilities; evaluate in AI2THOR kitchens (find / slice / clear)
Novelty

A modular LLM + cognitive-architecture bootstrap that curbs hallucination and generalizes.

Impact

More efficient, adaptable embodied agents that need minimal LLM help at runtime.

[7] “Bootstrapping Cognitive Agents with a Large Language Model,” AAAI 2024.
Insight 08 · LLM agents & applied foundation models

KG-TREAT: Treatment Effect Estimation by Synergizing Patient Data with Knowledge Graphs

KG-TREAT · AAAI 2024
Goal

Improve treatment-effect estimation (TEE) by combining patient data with biomedical knowledge graphs.

Challenge

Small labeled data and sparse, high-dimensional records; full KGs add noise and miss causal links.

Method
  • Dual-focus personalized KGs (treatment-covariate and outcome-covariate)
  • Deep bi-level attention synergy (DIVE) across covariates, treatments and outcomes
  • Pre-train with masked-code + link prediction, then fine-tune for TEE
Novelty

Dual-focus PKGs + bi-level attention deeply fuse patient data and knowledge graphs.

Impact

Beats baselines on AUC / AUPR / IF-PEHE — better, generalizable treatment-effect estimation.

[8] “KG-TREAT: Pre-training for Treatment Effect Estimation by Synergizing Patient Data with Knowledge Graphs,” AAAI 2024.
Insight 09 · Simulation, perception & autonomous driving

SPDiff: Social-Physics-Informed Diffusion Model for Crowd Simulation

SPDiff · AAAI 2024
Goal

Produce realistic, generalizable crowd simulation for urban planning and traffic.

Challenge

Physics models miss micro motion; data-driven methods don't generalize; trajectories are complex and heterogeneous.

Method
  • A conditional denoising diffusion model infused with Social-Force physics
  • Equivariant / invariant constraints on position, velocity and acceleration
  • Multi-frame rollout training for long horizons; a graph network for interactions
Novelty

Infuses physical knowledge and equivariance into a diffusion model for crowds.

Impact

More realistic, generalizable long-horizon crowd simulation.

[9] “Social Physics Informed Diffusion Model for Crowd Simulation,” AAAI 2024.
Insight 10 · Simulation, perception & autonomous driving

Vampire: Regulating Intermediate 3D Features for Vision-Centric Autonomous Driving

Vampire · AAAI 2024
Goal

Generate better dense 3D features for multi-camera autonomous-driving perception.

Challenge

Multi-camera perception struggles to produce dense, useful 3D features.

Method
  • LSS 2D→3D transform; a 3D hourglass inpaints sparse features into dense ones
  • Volume rendering as a regulator for dense 3D features (camera and bird's-eye view)
  • Signed-Distance-Function-modeled density + semantic volumes
Novelty

Uses volume rendering as a regulator for intermediate 3D features across tasks.

Impact

Competitive 3D occupancy, LiDAR segmentation and 3D detection from cameras alone.

[10] “Regulating Intermediate 3D Features for Vision-Centric Autonomous Driving,” AAAI 2024.
Insight 11 · Simulation, perception & autonomous driving

Accelerating AVs with the Next Generation of Generative AI (Keynote)

Raquel Urtasun (keynote) · Waabi
Goal

Rethink autonomous driving with scalable generative-AI simulation and foundation models.

Challenge

Real-world AV testing is labor- and capital-intensive; rare events are hard; the industry is consolidating.

Method
  • Deep structure models — scalable, affordable optimization
  • Waabi World: an AI simulator that builds digital twins from raw sensor data
  • Waabi Driver: an interpretable foundation model learning from simulation + real data
Novelty

Generative-AI simulation plus an interpretable, verifiable AV foundation model.

Impact

Faster, safer, more scalable AV deployment without endless real-world miles.

[11] R. Urtasun, “Accelerating AVs with the Next Generation of Generative AI,” AAAI 2024 (invited talk).
Insight 12 · Robust & efficient learning

Efficient Knowledge Transfer for Spiking Neural Networks from Static to Event Domain

SNN static→event transfer · AAAI 2024
Goal

Train spiking neural networks (SNNs) well on scarce event-based neuromorphic data.

Challenge

Event datasets are small and under-annotated → SNNs overfit; there is a static↔event domain mismatch.

Method
  • Use static images to assist SNN training
  • A knowledge-transfer loss: domain-alignment + spatio-temporal regularization
  • A sliding training strategy from static-invariant features to full event processing
Novelty

A domain-alignment + spatio-temporal transfer that fuses static and event features.

Impact

Better-generalizing, less-overfit SNNs for neuromorphic event vision.

[12] “An Efficient Knowledge Transfer Strategy for Spiking Neural Networks from Static to Event Domain,” AAAI 2024.
Insight 13 · Robust & efficient learning

Graph Invariant Learning with Subgraph Co-mixup for OOD Generalization

Graph invariant learning (co-mixup) · AAAI 2024
Goal

Make graph neural networks generalize under distribution shift (out-of-distribution).

Challenge

GNNs generalize poorly OOD; invariant learning needs diverse environments; mixup blurs invariant vs environment subgraphs.

Method
  • An invariant-subgraph extractor separates invariant vs environment subgraphs
  • Environment Mixup + Invariant Mixup generate diverse training environments
  • Retain only invariant information, removing spurious correlations
Novelty

Subgraph co-mixup combining invariant learning with environment mixing.

Impact

Stronger OOD generalization for molecular, protein and social graphs.

[13] “Graph Invariant Learning with Subgraph Co-mixup for Out-of-Distribution Generalization,” AAAI 2024.
Conclusions

Synthesis across the papers

Insights

  • LLMs dominate AAAI 2024, but the theme is reliability — citations (CoT + CIM), symbolic solvers (SYRELM), grounding (cognitive agents) and probing rationality limits.
  • Foundation / multimodal models reach high-stakes domains — pathology (PathAsst) and healthcare treatment effects with knowledge graphs (KG-TREAT).
  • Physics- and structure-informed generative models (SPDiff, Vampire, Waabi) bring realism and verifiability to simulation and autonomous driving.

Vision

  • Interpretable, verifiable foundation models (Urtasun / Waabi) over black boxes.
  • Hybrid neuro-symbolic and LLM + cognitive-architecture systems that curb hallucination.
  • Efficiency and robustness: frugal LMs, neuromorphic SNNs and OOD-robust GNNs.

Implications for us

  • Pair LLMs with retrieval, symbolic solvers and knowledge graphs for trustworthy, citeable outputs.
  • Use generative simulation and digital twins to cut real-world data and testing cost.
  • Invest in domain-adapted foundation models and OOD / robustness for deployment.
